Ticket two four one seven. Client: Robert. Problems: a delivery delay, a mistake in the invoice, and one damaged box. Solution: a new delivery date, a new invoice, and a refund for the box.
Hello, Karina. It is Robert. Did you read my email?
Yes, I did, Robert. I'm very sorry about the delay.
The jet is two weeks late, and we have a trip to Chicago on June first.
I understand. Let me check with the factory. The new delivery date is May twenty-sixth.
OK, that is before our trip. And the invoice?
You are right, the price was a mistake. I apologize. I'll send you a new invoice today.
Thank you. One box of spare parts was damaged, too.
I'm sorry about that. We'll send new parts this week, and we'll give you a refund for the box.
That is a good solution, Karina. Thank you for your help.
You're welcome, Robert. It won't happen again. I'll call you on Monday.

Hello, this is Daniel Cole from Blue Sky Charter in Miami. I am calling about our order. We received the aircraft yesterday, thank you. But there is a problem. In the contract, the seats are gray, and the seats in the aircraft are brown. Also, the manual is only in Portuguese, and our pilots need a manual in English. Please call me back today or tomorrow, before five p.m. Thank you, and have a good day.

Hi, it's Sofia from Texas again. In my business, problems happen. A delivery is late, or a document has a mistake. Here is what I do. First, I listen. I don't interrupt the client. Second, I say sorry: I'm sorry about the problem. Third, I offer a solution: Let me check, or I'll send you a new document today. And I always call the client back the next day. Last month, a client had a big problem with a delay. Now he is my best customer!

First, Robert writes an email about the problems with his order. Then, Karina reads the email and calls him. Next, she says: I'm sorry about the delay. After that, she checks the new delivery date with the factory. Finally, she sends a new invoice, and Robert is happy with the solution.
